title: FlashAttention: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Attention with IO-Awareness
authors: Tri Dao, Daniel Y. Fu, Stefano Ermon, Atri Rudra, Christopher Ré
lab: Stanford University (Hazy Research) and University at Buffalo, SUNY
date: May 2022 (arXiv v1); v2 June 2022; published at NeurIPS 2022

code.title: Dao-AILab/flash-attention
code.note: the authors' kernels, now FlashAttention-2 to 4, BSD 3-Clause licence (repo, about 25 minutes for the README and entry path)

takeaway: Exact attention made 2-7x faster and linear-memory by tiling + online softmax + backward recomputation in one fused CUDA kernel, proving HBM IO (not FLOPs) is the true cost of attention.
verdict: Believe the algorithm and the kernel benchmarks: exactness is proved, the IO argument is checkable, and every major framework has shipped it since. Treat the end-to-end training speedups and the long-context quality gains as single runs against baselines that were not always run like for like.

headline.k: 40.3 GB down to 4.4 GB, GPT-2 medium attention, forward + backward
headline.d: 5.7× faster although it does 13% more arithmetic

headline.k: than PyTorch attention at sequence length 4K
headline.d: memory linear in N; up to 3.3× faster for N = 128 to 2K

headline.k: the first Transformer above chance (50%) at 16K tokens

resources.n: the best gentle walkthrough of the tiling and rescaling math, with diagrams of the block loops.
derives the algorithm the right way round, starting from 3-pass safe softmax, then online softmax, then the fused one-pass attention; the cleanest path to reconstructing the kernel yourself.
the author's own explanation of the memory hierarchy argument and the algorithm.

resources.t: Making Deep Learning Go Brrrr From First Principles
resources.n: not about FlashAttention specifically, but the compute-bound against memory-bound framing that makes the whole paper obvious in retrospect.
the first author's papers and blog posts, including the FlashAttention-2 and -3 write-ups.

kb.n: 2017: the O(N²) attention this paper makes fast without changing its output.

kb.t: Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention
kb.n: 2023: the complementary inference-side memory result; FlashAttention optimises HBM to SRAM traffic inside the kernel, PagedAttention optimises KV-cache allocation across requests. Serving stacks use both.
2019: the training-systems baseline FlashAttention beats in Tables 2 and 4, and later integrated into (Megatron-LM pull request 267).

kb.t: Mamba: Linear-Time Sequence Modeling with Selective State Spaces
kb.n: 2023: Tri Dao's other line of attack on sequence length; its selective-scan kernel reuses the same IO-aware recipe (fuse, keep state in SRAM, recompute in backward).
2024, and every modern LLM report: FlashAttention-class kernels are assumed infrastructure for the published long-context and MFU numbers.
2018: BERT-large is the model of Table 1's 15% training-speed result.
2019: the other half of training memory; ZeRO shards the model states, FlashAttention removes the N × N activations.

topics.n: primary: the canonical fused kernel and IO-aware cost model.
